intro: **Earn the comparison.** 0.16.0 is the release where Iris can be opened beside any incumbent and every noun on the table is either shipped and measured or named as a gap in Iris's own words. A trace carries a session; a run can be a baseline and a comparison lists the cases the two runs disagree on; a moment fires a webhook; a CI job gets a one-line Action; Python gets a client and a pytest plugin; every OpenTelemetry framework gets a recipe bound to a fixture that proves it; every listing renders from the truthbase; the fourteen compare pages hold against the vendors' pages as they read today, with a cost-to-run row and a five-question FAQ; the response schema is published and locked; the verdict's decision path is exported; and how long an evaluation takes is measured rather than asserted.

- **`suggestions` is gone from every evaluation response**, deprecated in 0.13.0 and removed here on the two-minor schedule. Read `interpretations[]` (who the sentence is for, and the setting that changes it) and `rule_results[]` (the failing rules and each skip's reason) instead. The database column stays, written as `[]`, so a database 0.16.0 writes still opens on 0.15.0.
- **`docs/roadmap.md` is gone.** The capability map is the roadmap: `docs/capabilities.md` and https://iris-eval.com/capabilities. `iris-eval.com/roadmap` redirects there.

- **A trace's `session_id` is a column, not metadata.** Migration 014 adds it with its index on first start, beside 001–013. A trace that carried a session id in `metadata` keeps it there; new writes fill the column from `session_id`, `gen_ai.conversation.id`, or SEP-414 baggage.
- **Migration 013 adds `runs.baseline` and its partial unique index** — one baseline per agent, enforced by the database rather than by a read.
- **`notify.webhook` is strict like the rest of the configuration**: an unknown key refuses startup and names the nearest known one.
- **The compare pages carry a thirteenth row** (cost to run), so a tool that parsed the twelve-row table by position needs to read by `id`.

sections.title: Added
items: **The run comparison lists its discordant cases, and a run can be the baseline.** `compare_runs` and `POST /api/v1/compare` answer with `discordant[]` — the paired cases whose verdict flipped, regressions first, each with both evaluations, the direction and the rules that flipped (the b + c McNemar counts, named) — and `discordant_total`; the Runs page lists them under the comparison and each row opens the moment. `PATCH /api/v1/runs/:id { "baseline": true }` pins a run as the baseline (one per tenant, kept by a partial unique index — migration 013); `GET /api/v1/runs` carries `baseline`; an omitted `before` on `compare_runs` and `POST /api/v1/compare` means the pinned baseline, and the Runs page's compare form starts from it. The interval stays: nothing about the statistics changed.

**Sessions.** A trace carries `session_id` — explicit on `log_trace` and `POST /api/v1/traces`, or `gen_ai.conversation.id` on the OTLP door, or the SEP-414 baggage `session_id` when a request named nothing else — in a column with an index (migration 014). `get_traces` and `GET /api/v1/traces` filter by `session`; the trace drawer shows the session strip (which turn this is, the previous and the next, every turn linked); `compare_traces` takes `group_by: session`, so a conversation answered both ways reads as flaky. A sessions page is arc-10 work, once sessions exist in stored data.

**A webhook fires on a moment** (#5). `notify.webhook: { url, secret, events, cooldownMinutes, format, timeoutMs }` in the strict `config.json`, or `IRIS_WEBHOOK_URL` and `IRIS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Five events — `verdict_fail`, `detector_veto`, `cost_anomaly`, `regression_alarm` (the CUSUM line crossed at this evaluation), `flaky_case` (the first attempt that disagreed with every earlier one) — read from the store after the evaluation row is durable, whichever door wrote it, so nothing waits on the receiver. The body is the Standard Webhooks shape (`id`, `type`, `timestamp`, `data`) with the moment's ids, verdict, rules and numbers and never the agent's text; signed two ways any receiver already verifies (`webhook-id` / `webhook-timestamp` / `webhook-signature: v1,…` over `id.timestamp.body`, and `x-iris-signature: sha256=…` over the body); one attempt and three retries at 500 ms, 2 s, 8 s (±25%) on a network error, a timeout, 408, 429 or 5xx, then a logged drop; a cooldown per (event, agent, subject), ten minutes by default; a queue of a hundred. `format: slack` and `format: discord` post the bodies those services render. A typo'd event name, a non-http URL, or the `iris` format without a secret refuses startup naming it. `iris://capabilities` reports `notify.webhook` — events, host, format, signed — never the URL's token or the key. Found on the way: the strict schema's did-you-mean skipped keys under a `.nullable()` object; it unwraps those now. Guide: [docs/webhooks.md](docs/webhooks.md). Tests: `tests/unit/notify/{webhook,events,config,doors}.test.ts`.

**A GitHub Action for the CI gate.** `uses: iris-eval/mcp-server/.github/actions/gate@v0.16.0` with `traces: traces.ndjson` runs `iris-eval ingest --evaluate --fail-on …` (and `--dataset`), fails the job on the verdicts named, writes the receipt — trace ids, bases, rules, span labels, never the text — to the job summary, and on a pull request posts it as one comment updated in place (a marker names the traces file; a fork's read-only token, a missing permission or the comment turned off each skip it and say so; an empty traces file fails rather than passing green). A composite action with three small scripts and no third-party action to pin; dogfooded on this repository's CI (`gate-action`: the walk-through's leak caught inside the dataset, a clean file passing, the comment updated not duplicated). Guide: [docs/ci-gate.md](docs/ci-gate.md#github-actions--the-action-0160). Tests: `tests/ci-gate-action.test.ts`; the action file is held to the docs contract (flags, variables) and the unpublished-package scan.

**The Python client, `iris-eval` on PyPI** (#6). `packages/python`: `IrisClient` and `AsyncIrisClient` over `httpx` — `log_trace`, `evaluate_output` (through the ingest door with `evaluate: true`, so the output is stored and shows on the dashboard), `get_traces`, `get_trace`, `health`, `capabilities`; Bearer auth; typed answers (`iris_eval.types` mirrors the API reference key for key); a refusal raises `IrisError` with the server's own sentence, the status and the validation details; no server raises `IrisConnectionError` with the recipe. The server is found from `IRIS_URL` or the running dashboard's `runtime.json`, verified with the health route. A pytest plugin registers itself: the `iris` fixture (skips with the recipe when no server is there, fails with `IRIS_REQUIRE=1`) and `assert_iris(output, expect="pass")`, which asserts on the verdict's state and reads like the dashboard when it fails. CI runs the client's contract test against a keyed server this checkout builds on Python 3.10–3.13 and installs the wheel into a fresh environment; `publish-python.yml` publishes by PyPI trusted publishing on a `py-v*` tag once the project and the publisher are registered (the founder's item). A decorator SDK is deliberately not shipped: Iris reads the OpenTelemetry traces a Python framework already emits. Tests: `packages/python/tests`.

**The OTel recipes page.** `docs/otel-recipes.md`: one recipe per framework — Pydantic AI, Google ADK, LangGraph via LangSmith's export, CrewAI via OpenInference, AutoGen, Microsoft Agent Framework, Semantic Kernel, Vercel AI SDK, Mastra — the vendor's own setup lines (read from the page each recipe cites) with Iris as the OTLP endpoint, what Iris reads out of that vocabulary, and the fixture in this repository that proves the reading; where the fixture proves the vocabulary and not the framework's own capture (AutoGen, Mastra), the recipe says so. Held by `tests/docs-otel-recipes.test.ts`: every recipe names a fixture that exists, every convention fixture is named by a recipe, every recipe cites its source and points at the door; the page is in `llms.txt` and linked from the OTel guide and the README.

**Every listing inherits the truth.** `server.json` carries `title`, `websiteUrl` and `icons` (the SVG and the PNG the site serves), validated against the vendored 2025-12-11 registry schema in `tests/listings-hygiene.test.ts`; the README's works-with table is rendered from `clients.json` through the truthbase (a block `npm run llms:render` rewrites and `llms:check` holds); an Install-in-VS-Code button and the Cursor button in its current install form, both registering the server as `iris-eval`; the mcp.so badge on the listing's real address; a Docker MCP Catalog entry (`docs/launch/listings/docker/server.yaml`, with its copy) ready for the registry pull request; a Cursor plugin manifest (`.cursor-plugin/plugin.json`, on the version gates) so the repository installs as a Cursor plugin; `smithery.yaml` retired with its reason (Smithery lists a local server as an MCPB bundle now, and the file's docs page returned 404); `localhost:3838` → `localhost:6920` in the site's two mockups, held by the test; the historical launch drafts held to their "do not repost" banners; and **a demo GIF at the top of the README** — the demo database landing on Failures, a failure opened, two runs compared — recorded by `scripts/demo-media.mts` (Playwright video → ffmpeg), under 3 MB and asserted so, with the MP4 source at `website/public/demo.mp4`.

**The compare pages hold against today's vendor pages.** Every vendor cell's sentence is checked against a plain download of its page by `npm run compare:verify` (`scripts/verify-compare-quotes.mjs`), which now reads a page the way a reader would — inline Markdown markup gone, since most vendors' docs answer a plain fetch with Markdown, and the spacing a stripped tag leaves before punctuation closed — and `--write` records `quoteVerified` and `quotesCheckedOn` in the files. Twenty-two cells corrected from a second read of the vendors' pages (Langfuse's server-side code evaluators, Weave's Signals, Judgment's `evaluate_traces` and `run_test`, Promptfoo's trajectory and tool-call assertions, Opik's 40+ metrics, Phoenix MCP named, Patronus's judge evaluator, CoreWeave's completed acquisition of Weights & Biases on its own page). A thirteenth row, **Cost to run**, on every comparison, read from the vendor's pricing page and dated, or saying the vendor's pages do not answer. A five-question FAQ on every page in the buyer's words — two written, three derived from the table so the FAQ cannot say what the table does not — emitted as FAQPage JSON-LD too; a playground link in the call to action. The four-way article, "Iris vs Langfuse vs Phoenix vs Promptfoo: where each wins, where each loses", drafted with every vendor statement linked to a page its compare file lists as a source, held unpublished by `published: false` and a future date; the Dev.to crossposter now honours `published: false`. `tests/compare-contract.test.ts`, `tests/compare-quote-verifier.test.ts` and `tests/compare-article-draft.test.ts` hold all of it.

**The verdict says which layer decided, and now you can read the whole path.** `verdictPath(result, config)` returns the composer's decision node by node — a configured gate, a detector's veto, a critical check that could not answer, evidence the deployment requires, the risk estimate — each naming what it found and whether it decided. `compose()` reads the node that decided and stamps the verdict from it, so the two cannot disagree; a path stops at the decider, because the layers after it were never asked. Exported from `@iris-eval/mcp-server/engine` with the `VerdictNode` type, and asserted in the packed-and-installed probe CI runs.

**The response schema is published and locked.** `https://iris-eval.com/response-schema-v1.json` — JSON Schema 2020-12, rendered from the same zod schema `evaluate_output` validates its answer against (`npm run schema:render`), so a client generating types or validating a stored response reads what the server actually returns. A test renders it and fails when the committed file has drifted, and validates a response the engine produced against it.

**How long an evaluation takes is measured and published.** `npm run proof` now times `EvalEngine.evaluateAll` — the call `evaluate_output` makes — over every case in the proof corpus, discards a warm-up and reports p50 and p95 with the machine that produced them, on the proof page and in `proof/RESULTS.md`. It is excluded from `proof --check` (latency is a property of the machine, and CI's runner is not your laptop) and the hardcoded-claim scanner's new `eval-latency` pattern refuses a number anywhere that disagrees with the truthbase.

**OTLP traces arrive as protobuf too.** `POST /v1/traces` accepts `application/x-protobuf` beside `application/json` — the Python OTLP exporter's only encoding, so until now no Python framework (Pydantic AI, Google ADK, LangGraph via LangSmith's export, CrewAI, AutoGen, Microsoft's Agent Framework) reached the door without a Collector between. The decoder is `src/otel/protobuf.ts`: a wire-format reader for the one message Iris accepts, about two hundred lines and no dependency (against `protobufjs` at 3.8 MB and `@bufbuild/protobuf` at 1.9 MB), producing exactly the OTLP/JSON object the JSON path already parses, so the mapping and every test below it are unchanged. Held to the real thing: `tests/fixtures/otlp/*.pb` are the request bodies `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http` 1.44.0 posted, and the decoder must reproduce their JSON twins byte for byte. Any other content type is a 415 naming both encodings; a malformed protobuf body is a 400 with the byte offset. gRPC is still not served — `docs/otel-integration.md` carries the one-file Collector bridge.

**The OTLP door speaks every convention a buyer will test.** Beside the GenAI conventions it already read, `POST /v1/traces` now reads OpenInference (`input.value`, `output.value`, `llm.token_count.*`, `llm.model_name`, `session.id`, `openinference.span.kind`), OpenLLMetry (`traceloop.entity.input` / `output`, `traceloop.span.kind`, `llm.request.type`, the indexed `gen_ai.prompt.N.content`), LangSmith's export (`langsmith.span.kind`), Semantic Kernel's `gen_ai.response.prompt_tokens` / `completion_tokens`, and the Vercel AI SDK's legacy `ai.prompt` / `ai.response.text` / `ai.usage.*` / `ai.model.id` / `ai.toolCall.*`; `gen_ai.agent.name` names the agent before the `"otel"` default; the model lands in `metadata.model` (what the judge's same-family check reads), `gen_ai.conversation.id` in `metadata.session_id`, and `gen_ai.tool.definitions` in `tools[]` for `valid_tool_arguments`. **Token usage is summed over the leaf carriers only** — a framework that puts the run's totals on `invoke_agent` beside `chat` children that carry their own (Microsoft Agent Framework, the Vercel SDK's `generateText` over its `doGenerate`) is counted once, where every span used to be added; Pydantic AI's whole-run `gen_ai.aggregated_usage.*` wins when present. One fixture per framework, authored to the vendor's documentation, holds each of these (`tests/fixtures/otlp/conventions/`).

**Trace context is carried (SEP-414).** `log_trace` and `evaluate_output` read W3C `traceparent` / `tracestate` / `baggage` from the request's `_meta` (and the MCP session id from the transport), and `POST /api/v1/traces` and `POST /v1/traces` from the headers of the same names; what arrived is stored under `metadata.trace_context` (the header, the trace id, the caller's parent span id, the sampled flag, the session id) — `evaluate_output` writes it onto its linked trace when that trace has none. The API returns it and the trace drawer shows it. A root that joined the caller's trace also carries `mcp.method.name` and `mcp.session.id` per the OTel MCP conventions. A trace stored with a context is exported to `IRIS_OTEL_ENDPOINT` under the caller's trace id with its root parented to the caller's span, so Iris's evaluation appears inside the agent's own trace in Langfuse, Phoenix, Logfire or Jaeger. Without a context nothing changes. Claude Code sends `_meta` as null on `tools/call` (anthropics/claude-code#76391), so from that client the capture plugin is the session link.

**Expected-trajectory rules, measured — and an off-task answer no longer reads clean.** Four built-in rules (25 now), each with a corpus family and its precision and recall on the proof page. `tool_sequence` compares the calls the caller expected (`expected_trajectory.tool_calls` on `evaluate_output`) with the calls made, in a mode — `strict`, `unordered`, `subset`, `superset` or `ordered_subset` (the default; a two-pointer subsequence check) — matching by tool name and, when the expectation names arguments, by `exact` or `subset` input; `step_budget` holds the call count to the budget the caller stated for THIS task (`expected_trajectory.step_budget`, or the number of expected calls) times a tolerance (default 1.5); both are policies that gate because the caller stated the expectation, and both skip without one. `tool_choice` finds the wrong tool for the ask from the catalogue `valid_tool_arguments` already takes: it scores the ask's actionable terms (the ones some tool's name, description or input properties mention) against each tool and fires when an uncalled tool fits at least 0.5 and beats the tools called by at least 0.34 — a heuristic detection that lowers the score and never vetoes. **`answers_the_ask` answers the composer question:** a truncated or off-topic answer read `passed: true, basis: clean` because the two relevance rules are measurements, which inform the score, and only policies and detections gate. Measured on the 141-case composite corpus before the rule existed, gating on both measurements failing together flipped no classless clean case, caught four of the eight off-task cases and six stub cases the composer missed — so the pair now decides: `answers_the_ask` is a policy with no number of its own — when the input is present and both `keyword_overlap` and `topic_consistency` fail at their thresholds, the output answers something else and the verdict fails on `policy_gate`, at the shipped defaults too. It skips whenever either measurement skips and on an ask with fewer than two content terms; a right answer that reuses none of the ask's words reads as off task (three of the corpus' twenty-five negatives), and the two measurements' thresholds are the knob. Two failure classes join the vocabulary (`wrong_trajectory`, `wrong_tool`) and one need (`expected_trajectory`); `off_task` joins the composite corpus' tier A, so the composite is regenerated. The capability map's Q3×S3 and Q4×S3 move from gap to has with evidence that resolves.

sections.title: Fixed
items: **Two processes opening one cold database at the same instant no longer lose one of them on the WAL switch.** `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` upgrades the connection's SHARED lock to EXCLUSIVE, and SQLite does not run the busy handler on that upgrade (two connections each waiting for the other's SHARED lock would never return), so the 0.14.0 fix — the timeout set before the switch — covered a plain wait and never this one: the losing process still failed with `database is locked` whatever `busy_timeout` said. The adapter now retries the switch itself with a short backoff inside the same five-second budget, on either driver's busy error; an error that is not BUSY is thrown as it came, and a failed boot closes the handle. Found by arc 9's N-10 CI run on the Node 22 built-in driver.

**`passed` means one thing across the four eval tools.** `evaluate_with_llm_judge` and `verify_citations` stored one judgment row each and reported their own pass/fail beside it, so a stored judgement read back with no verdict at all (the composer derives a verdict on read only from a row that carries provenance) and the two tools' `passed` was the threshold's word where every other surface's was the composer's (#375 item 2). Both rows now go through the engine's composer before they are stored — provenance and all — and both responses carry the composer's `verdict` (`state`, `basis`, `by`), the same object `evaluate_output` prints: a failed judgment gates (`policy_gate` by the judge), a passed one is `clean`, and a citation check that judged nothing is `unknown` (`no_rules`), never a pass. `tests/unit/tools/judge-verdict.test.ts` drives both tools through the MCP surface with the model mocked and reads the rows back.

**The demo is the engine's own output.** `--demo` used to write hand-shaped evaluations — a failing card read `FAIL · Fail:` with nothing after the colon, a FAIL card said `2/2 pass`, Runs was empty, the Audit Log was empty and Drift had no prior period. Now every seeded trace is stored and judged through the same function `log_trace`, `POST /api/v1/traces` and `ingest` call, dated when the trace happened, so a demo row carries exactly what a real one does: the verdict with its basis, the evidence spans, the interpretations, the provenance. The traffic spans two weeks (the Drift view's default window has the week before it), two runs on the same twelve questions are seeded with a `release-gate` dataset over them (the bad deployment shipped unfilled templates; the comparison shows the recovery with an interval), the demo's two custom rules go through the real store (one enabled and firing, one paused, three audit rows), and the injection case is one the rule actually judges — a hidden directive in a forum post the summarizer complied with, not a quoted phrase the rule rightly reads as discussion. The three LLM-judge rows keep canned scores (the judge needs a key) but are built by the judge tool's own row builder, now one function (`src/eval/llm-judge/persisted.ts`).

**The dashboard's top bar holds at phone width.** Below 768 px the command-palette trigger ("Search or jump to… Ctrl K") ran under the status chips (`live`, `judge off`, `DEMO`) on every page. The trigger is now its icon at that width (the accessible name and the shortcut are unchanged), the title row wraps its chips onto a second line, and the header grows to fit — nothing overlaps and every chip stays visible, because the chips carry live state a phone reader still needs. `tests/e2e/header-phone.spec.ts` measures it: on four pages of a demo server at 400 × 820, no two top-bar children share a pixel and nothing runs past the right edge.

**The read routes refuse a misspelled filter.** Every dashboard GET query schema was a bare `z.object`, which strips an unknown parameter, so `GET /api/v1/moments?agent_nme=docs-qa` returned every agent's rows exactly as if the filter had applied — the silent-strip defect the mutating bodies were cured of in 0.5.x (#376), one verb over. The thirteen query schemas (`/traces`, `/evals`, `/runs`, `/cases`, `/summary`, `/eval-stats` and its `/trend`, `/drift` and `/failures`, `/failures`, `/moments`, `/audit`, `/labels`, `/issues`) are now strict: an unknown parameter is a 400 naming it and the valid ones. **Observable for an API caller:** a request that sent an extra or misspelled query parameter and got a page back now gets a 400 — check the parameter names against `docs/architecture.md`.

**Every README link survives the npm package.** The package ships `dist`, `LICENSE`, `README.md` and `server.json`, so a relative link to `docs/` or a sibling package was dead for everyone reading the README from `node_modules` (#369 item 1). The last four relative links are absolute, and `tests/docs-contract.test.ts` refuses any README link that is relative to a file the package does not carry.

**`POST /api/v1/rules/custom` deploys an `action_policy`.** The route's own copy of the rule-type enum stopped at eight types while `deploy_rule` accepted nine, so the policy that gates a deploy could be deployed over MCP and not over HTTP (found by the 0.15.0 stranger's gate phase). The list is one exported constant (`RULE_TYPE_VALUES`) the store, the tool and the route all build from; `tests/unit/dashboard/routes/rules-action-policy.test.ts` deploys one rule of every type over HTTP and reads them back. `docs/ci-gate.md` step 1 shows the config-file form beside the env form — a session that cannot prefix a command with a variable starts the same refusal through `--config gate.json` — and the walk-through test runs that form.

**The dashboard's poll no longer discards a slow response.** A poll tick that fired while the previous request was still in flight took the request id, so the pending response was dropped as stale — and the next one, and the next. On a server with enough traffic that a 200-moment window took longer than the cadence, the Drift and Health prior windows never rendered and the banner said "No prior period to compare against yet" over two weeks of data. A tick now waits for the request in flight (a manual refetch still supersedes); the Drift, Health and agent-list reads poll at the normal cadence rather than the live tail's; the change banner says it is comparing while a window loads instead of claiming there is nothing to compare; and the moments and failures routes hydrate a page's evaluations in one batched read (`getEvalsByTraceIds`) instead of one query per trace.

sections.title: Changed
items: **`no_tool_loop` catches a repeating cycle of any length.** The cycle clause stopped at period 3 ("beyond three the pattern is a plan, not a loop"), so a four-call block repeated three times over — twelve calls that between them asked four questions three times, every answer unchanged — walked straight through (#427). The period searched is now bounded by what can still repeat more than the allowance inside the trajectory (`maxCycleLength(n) = floor(n / 3)`): a plan repeated twice is a retry and passes; the same plan a third time is the machine stuck. The polling exemption and the shorter-period rule are unchanged. Two corpus cases pin both sides (`loop-041` fails, `loop-042` passes); the family measures n = 42, precision 1.00, recall 1.00 on corpus `a2825049eb4f` (it was n = 40, 1.00 / 1.00 — nothing that fired stops firing, nothing that passed starts). **Observable:** an agent whose trajectory repeats a block of four or more distinct calls three times over is now judged a loop where it was not.

sections.title: Removed
items: **`suggestions` is gone, on the schedule 0.13.0 announced.** Every line it carried was a restatement of a field the same response already had — the failing rules (`rule_results`), the veto (`verdict.basis` `detector_veto` with `critical_failures`), each skip and its reason (`rule_results[].skipped` and `.skipReason`), the critical checks that could not judge (`critical_skipped`) — and a second copy of a verdict is a second verdict. `interpretations[]`, which has carried the sentences since 0.13.0, says who each one is for and which setting changes it; two sentences that only `suggestions` used to carry are now written there: when nothing was judged, and when a critical check skipped without making the verdict unknown. **Check before upgrading:** if you read `suggestions` from `evaluate_output`, from `POST /api/v1/traces` with `evaluate: true`, or from a stored row, read `interpretations[]` and `rule_results[]` instead. The `suggestions` column stays in the database, written as `[]`, so a database this version writes still opens on 0.15.0.

**`docs/roadmap.md` is gone; the capability map is the roadmap.** It said in prose what `docs/capabilities.md` says from the truthbase, and it went stale between releases — it still listed OpenTelemetry ingest and datasets as open a release after both shipped. `iris-eval.com/roadmap` redirects to `/capabilities`, the links that pointed at the file point at the map, and a test holds that no live surface links it and that the tracks on the site do not call shipped work planned.
